contribution.position: I hold my reliability position, and the evidence now has a conflict that needs resolving. QA (axis:risk) says artifact:perf-report shows p99_latency of 180ms, comfortably inside the 250ms budget. The artifact says otherwise: p99_latency measured 410ms at peak load against a 250ms budget. QA's figure does not appear in any listed artifact, so I cannot accept 'risk is contained' on that basis. Either QA is citing a different run that is not in the artifact list, or the number is misquoted. QA should produce that run, with its load profile and code path, or retract the figure. Ops (axis:operability) says artifact:ops-runbook documents deploy and rollback steps. I accept that as far as it goes. The runbook text only covers deploy and rollback, and nothing in it addresses retry-storm mitigation or client backoff. Rollback is therefore a recovery path, not evidence that the 410ms overrun will not trigger the retry-storm failure mode behind the two sev2 incidents in artifact:incident-log. Product's cost finding (+3% against a 5% ceiling) is not in dispute and does not bear on reliability. The test report (412 passed, 0 failed) is functional and does not speak to peak-load behavior. Still missing, with no artifact in the list: (a) whether 410ms comes from the changed code path or the test environment, (b) the client retry and backoff configuration and whether it is bounded at that latency, and (c) a repeat load test within budget, or a documented and approved exception.
